'''Robert Schrader''' (12 September 1939 – 29 November 2015)<ref name="obit">{{cite journal |author=Knauf, Andreas|author2=Potthoff, Jürgen Potthoff|author3=Schmidt, Martin |url=http://www.iamp.org/bulletins/old-bulletins/Bulletin-April2016-print.pdf |title=Obituary. Robert Schrader (1939–2015) |journal=IAMP News Bulletin (Iamp.org)|pages=23–28|date=April 2016  }} [http://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/mueller/people/Obituary.pdf text of obituary at math.uni-bonn.de]</ref> was a German theoretical and mathematical physicist and professor of the [[Free University of Berlin]]. He is known for the [[Osterwalder–Schrader axioms]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Jorgensen, Palle E. T.|author2=Olafsson, Gestur|title=Osterwalder-Schrader axioms-Wightman axioms|date=2000|eprint=math-ph/0001010 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Robert Schrader was born in Berlin, Germany in 1939.<ref name="obit" />

From 1959 to 1964 Schrader studied physics at [[Kiel University]], the [[University of Zurich]], and the [[University of Hamburg]], where he completed his [[Diplom]] in 1964. His Diplom thesis ''Die Charaktere der inhomogenen Lorentzgruppe'' (The [[Character (mathematics)|character]]s of the inhomogeneous [[Lorentz group]]) was supervised by [[Harry Lehmann]] and [[Hans Joos]]. In 1965 he went to [[ETH Zurich]], where he worked as an assistant and received his doctorate ([[Promotion (Germany)|''Promotion'']]) in 1969 under the supervision of [[Klaus Hepp]] and [[Res Jost]].<ref name="obit" /> His thesis, published in ''[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]'', dealt with the Lee model introduced in 1954 by [[Tsung-Dao Lee]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=93917|name=Robert Schrader}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Schrader, R.|year=1968|title=On the existence of a local Hamiltonian in the Galilean invariant Lee model|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=10|issue=2 |pages=155–178|doi=10.1007/BF01654239 |bibcode=1968CMaPh..10..155S |s2cid=189832827 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01654239|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.95.1329 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.95.1329 |title=Some Special Examples in Renormalizable Field Theory |year=1954 |last1=Lee |first1=T. D. |journal=Physical Review |volume=95 |issue=5 |pages=1329–1334 |bibcode=1954PhRv...95.1329L |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=2001.07781 |doi=10.1088/1742-6596/1612/1/012012 |title=The Lee model: A tool to study decays |year=2020 |last1=Giacosa |first1=Francesco |journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series |volume=1612 |issue=1 |article-number=012012 |bibcode=2020JPhCS1612a2012G |s2cid=210859101 }}</ref>

From 1970 to 1973 Schrader was a research fellow at [[Harvard University]] and at [[Princeton University]]. At Harvard under the supervision of [[Arthur Jaffe]], he worked with [[Konrad Osterwalder]] on Euclidean quantum field theory. In 1971 Schrader [[Habilitation|habilitated]] at the University of Hamburg with the thesis ''Das Yukawa Modell in zwei Raum-Zeit-Dimensionen'' (The [[Yukawa model]] in two space-time dimensions). He was a professor of theoretical physics at the [[Free University of Berlin]] from 1973 until his retirement in 2005. He was a visiting scientist in 1974 and again in 1980 at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|IHÉS]] at [[Paris]], in 1976 in Harvard, in 1979 at [[CERN]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Scharader |first=R. |year=1980 |title=High energy behaviour for non-relativistic scattering by stationary external metrics and Yang-Mills potentials |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01477304 |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik C |language=en |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=27–36 |doi=10.1007/BF01477304 |bibcode=1980ZPhyC...4...27S |issn=0170-9739|url-access=subscription }}</ref> for the academic year 1986/87 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and in 1989 at the ETH. For two academic years from 1982 to 1984, he was a visiting professor at the [[Stony Brook University|State University of New York at Stony Brook]].<ref name=obit/>

Schrader was the author or coauthor of more than 100 scientific publications.<ref name=obit/> He dealt with [[axiomatic quantum field theory]] and, with Konrad Osterwalder, introduced in 1973 the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for Euclidean [[Green's function]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Osterwalder, Konrad|author2=Schrader, Robert|year=1973|pages=83–112|title=Axioms for Euclidean Green's functions| url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01645738|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=31|issue=2 |doi=10.1007/BF01645738 |bibcode=1973CMaPh..31...83O |s2cid=189829853 |url-access=subscription}} (over 1350 citations)</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Osterwalder, Konrad|author2=Schrader, Robert|year=1975|pages=281–305|title=Axioms for Euclidean Green's functions II|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01608978|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=42|issue=3 |doi=10.1007/BF01608978 |bibcode=1975CMaPh..42..281O |s2cid=119389461 |url-access=subscription}} (over 850 citations)</ref> Arthur Jaffe suggested to his postdocs Osterwalder and Schrader that they study the work on the Euclidean formulation of [[quantum field theory]] (QFT) done by [[Kurt Symanzik]] and [[Edward Nelson]]. The two postdocs published a set of axioms, which contained the crucial property called reflection positivity (RP), also referred to as Osterwalder–Schrader positivity. The Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction theorem states that the [[Wightman function]]s of a relativistic QFT can be reconstructed from the [[Schwinger function]]s of a Euclidean theory satisfying the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. RP is important for [[statistical mechanics]] and [[lattice gauge theory]].<ref name=obit/> Schrader worked on many other areas of mathematical and theoretical physics, such as [[Yang–Mills theory]],<ref>{{cite journal|author=Cotta-Ramusino, P.|author2=Krüger, W.|author3=Schrader, R.|year=1979|title=Quantum scattering by external metrics and Yang–Mills potentials|journal=Annales de |first2=Michael E. |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=92 |issue=4 |pages=555–594 |bibcode=1984CMaPh..92..555S |s2cid=121255055 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(78)90228-6 |title=A conjecture on the spinor functional determinant |year=1978 |last1=Hogreve |first1=H. |last2=Schrader |first2=R. |last3=Seiler |first3=R. |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=142 |issue=4 |pages=525–534 |bibcode=1978NuPhB.142..525H }}</ref> invariants of three-dimensional manifolds,<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/25/18/018 |title=State sum invariants of compact 3-manifolds with boundary and 6j-symbols |year=1992 |last1=Karowski |first1=M. |last2=Muller |first2=W. |last3=Schrader |first3=R. |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General |volume=25 |issue=18 |pages=4847–4860 |bibcode=1992JPhA...25.4847K }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|eprint=hep-th/9310054 |last1=Mund |first1=J. |last2=Schrader |first2=R. journal|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(84)91494-1 |title=On the electromagnetic response to gravitational waves |year=1984 |last1=Schrader |first1=Robert |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=143 |issue=4–6 |pages=421–426 |bibcode=1984PhLB..143..421S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=1510.06376 |doi=10.1088/1751-8113/49/21/215202 |title=Reflection positivity in simplicial gravity |year=2016 |last1=Schrader |first1=Robert |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical |volume=49 |issue=21 |article-number=215202 |bibcode=2016JPhA...49u5202S |s2cid=119633988 }}</ref> [[quantum Theories of Elementary Particles |series=Lecture Notes in Physics |year=1982 |last1=Cheeger |first1=J. |last2=Müller |first2=W. |last3=Schrader |first3=R. |volume=160 |pages=176–188 |isbn=978-3-540-11560-1 }}</ref>
His extensive collaboration with Vadim Korstrykin included research on [[quantum wire]]s<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/32/4/006 |title=Kirchhoff's rule for quantum wires |year=1999 |last1=Kostrykin |first1=V. |last2=Schrader |first2=R. |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General |volume=32 |issue=4 |pages=595–630 |arxiv=math-ph/9806013 |bibcode=1999JPhA...32..595K |s2cid=5186409 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Kostrykin, V.|author2=Schrader, R.|year=2000|title=Kirchhoff's rule for quantum wires. II: The inverse problem with possible applications to quantum computers|journal=Fortschritte der Physik |volume=48|issue=8|pages=703–716|doi=10.1002/1521-3978(200008)48:8<703::AID-PROP703>3.0.CO;2-O |arxiv=quant-ph/9910053 |bibcode=2000ForPh..48..703K |s2cid=17962858 }}</ref> and Laplacian operators on [[Quantum graph#Metric graphs|metric graphs]].<ref>{{cite book | chapter=''Laplacians on metric graphs: eigenvalues, resolvents and semigroups'' by Vadim Kostrykin and Robert Schrader | publisher=American Mathematical Society | location=Providence, Rhode Island | year=2006 | issn=1098-3627 | doi=10.1090/conm/415/07870 | pages=201–225|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J65sAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA201 | title=Quantum Graphs and Their Applications: Proceedings of an AMS-IMS-SIAM Joint Summer Research Conference on Quantum Graphs and Their Applications, June 19-23, 2005, Snowbird, Utah | isbn=978-0-8218-3765-8 | s2cid=9823477 | editor=Berkolaiko, Gregory }}</ref>

He died from cancer in 2015.<ref name="obit" />
